acceptance_criteria: v3 runs as a tampines library driven by a digital-twin GUI binary; passes the same TUAS CIET regression tests; hits real time; and the EXISTING ciet_v2_opcua_client drives it without modification.
description:
Maintainer direction 2026-08-13. Third generation of the CIET educational simulator.

ARCHITECTURE (as directed):
  - The SIMULATOR IS A LIBRARY and lives in crates/tampines.
  - The GUI BINARY lives in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine.
  - This split already matches the twin crate's own rule that it carries NO physics.

WHAT CHANGES vs v2:
  - Replace the TUAS array backend with OPCPFluidArray.
  - New widget art for heater, shell-and-tube heat exchanger, cooling fans, pump and piping, all on the new widget libraries.
  - Real-time capable, with an OPC-UA server that FITS THE EXISTING CLIENT unchanged.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS - verified by grep 2026-08-13, so none of this is greenfield:

  1. CIET v2 IS SUBSTANTIAL AND SHIPPING. Two binaries in the twin crate:
       ciet_educational_simulator_v2  (src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/)
       ciet_v2_opcua_client           (src/bin/ciet_v2_opcua_client/)
     plus src/ciet_opcua/ at 2,965 lines - state.rs 707, node_map.rs 746, simulator.rs 588, pki_paths.rs 200, server.rs 184, discovery.rs 71, user_controls.rs, mod.rs. The reactor-agnostic half (transport, server thread, tokio runtime, PKI, mDNS, address space, read/write callbacks) is already factored out into src/opcua_core/ and explicitly documented as serving ANY OUTRAM PARK simulator. v3 supplies its own half of that contract; it does not rewrite opcua_core.

  2. THERMINOL IS ALREADY IN THE COOLPROP FORK (maintainer was right): crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/incompressibles/ carries Therminol, with tests (incompressible_t66.rs, incompressible_freeze_psat.rs). No new fluid-property implementation should be written for the CIET coolant.

  3. OPCPFluidArray LIVES IN THE COOLPROP FORK, at src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/, and is already consumed by tampines-steam-tables. crates/tampines ALREADY depends on outram-park-fork-coolprop, so the dependency edge for this migration exists today.

  4. WIDGETS THAT ALREADY EXIST in the twin crate components/: heat_exchanger.rs, pump.rs, pipe.rs, pipe_component.rs, bend.rs, valve.rs, cooling_tower.rs. MISSING: a heater widget, and a cooling-FAN widget (cooling_tower is not the same thing).

  5. THE RE-VALIDATION TARGET EXISTS: tuas .../ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/regression_tests.rs plus the coupled-DRACS natural-circulation suite. v3 must pass the SAME tests.

NAME COLLISION - MUST BE RESOLVED BEFORE ANY CODE (see child bead): 'version_3' ALREADY MEANS SOMETHING ELSE. tuas .../ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/version_3/mod.rs (1,435 lines) is v2's PID control with branch mass flowrates on separate threads - a thread-parallelism variant, not this new generation. Two different things called v3 in one workspace will cause real confusion.

AI-drafted capture of maintainer direction; nothing here is validated.
title: CIET educational simulator v3 — tampines library + digital-twin GUI, OPCPFluidArray-backed

description:
A REAL PANIC BUG, not a documentation issue. Found 2026-08-11 while building the bounds-checked facade for op-t647; the facade had to exclude the point rather than fix it, because the fix belongs in the router.

THE DEFECT. In region_fwd_eqn_single_phase, the Region-2 and Region-3 dispatch arms use a HALF-OPEN pressure range `..100e6`. So p = 100 MPa exactly matches no arm and falls through the match, panicking, for any T above 623.15 K. At or below 623.15 K the point is accepted, so the failure is temperature-dependent and easy to miss.

THE KNOCK-ON, WHICH IS WORSE. Every (p,h) call at exactly 100 MPa panics, regardless of enthalpy — because the 1073.15 K isotherm helper internally evaluates h_tp_eqm_single_phase(1073.15 K, p), which lands in the broken arm. So the entire (p,h) family has an exclusive pressure ceiling for a reason that has nothing to do with (p,h).

100 MPa is the upper pressure bound of the IAPWS-IF97 validity region, so this is exactly the boundary a caller sweeping to the edge of the envelope will hit, and exactly the value someone writes when testing limits.

LIKELY FIX: `..100e6` should be `..=100e6` in the Region-2 and Region-3 arms. Verify against IAPWS-IF97 whether 100 MPa is inclusive in the standard (it is the stated upper limit, so it should be), then check every other range literal in the router for the same half-open/closed slip. Add a test that walks the exact envelope corners — p_min, p_max, T_min, T_max and their combinations — since that is the class of case no existing test covers.

INTERIM STATE: interfaces::checked (landed in commit 4feb6c84) documents and excludes the point, returning a typed error rather than panicking. That makes the facade safe but leaves the underlying router wrong, so anything calling the raw functions is still exposed.
title: tampines-steam-tables: IF97 region router PANICS at exactly p = 100 MPa above 623.15 K

description: gpu module (op-u6s.3) currently has one kernel (batched pointwise XS interpolation). Candidate follow-on embarrassingly-parallel kernels named in the design: delta-tracking (Woodcock) majorant evaluation over an energy array, and batched free-flight / collision-distance sampling. Same pattern: CPU f64 trusted reference + WGSL f32 accelerated path + GPU~=CPU-or-SKIP test.
title: outram-mc: additional GPU MC sub-kernels (delta-tracking majorant eval, batched free-flight sampling)

description: Wire optional wgpu 29 GPU compute into njoy for an embarrassingly-parallel WMP kernel. Target-gated (absent on Android -> pure CPU). gpu::probe() -> Option<GpuContext>; None => CPU. Demonstrator: batched WMP curve-fit polynomial background eval (real-valued, per-energy independent). CPU is the trusted/deterministic reference; GPU f32 is acceleration only. Full Faddeeva pole-sum WGSL port is TODO. AI draft -> docs/ai-fleet-review/njoy-wgpu/REVIEW_MANIFEST.md.
